start_here: Say to your AI: "Get the words said in the video at https://videos.example.com/watch?v=sample, from its captions if it has them." It runs tool:hear-a-link and hands back the title, the text and timed segments.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of its own: it reads one link and answers its words; any heard sound is kept as a file, not a list row.
instructions: 1. Install a link reader such as yt-dlp on your computer; for pages with no captions also keep whisper-cli, ffmpeg and a ggml Whisper model file.
2. Say "Get the words of the video at <link>", and give the link as url (add model_path for a page that has no captions).
3. The AI runs tool:hear-a-link with {url}; the page's own captions win, otherwise its sound is fetched and heard here and kept in /Heard links unless keep_sound is false.
4. Read what comes back: url, title, duration_seconds, text, segments, language, source (captions or heard). A link with no words fails and says why.

worked_examples.title: A link with captions is answered from its captions without hearing the sound
worked_examples.ask: Get the words said in the video at https://videos.example.com/watch?v=sample.
worked_examples.given: From the sample-run in tools/audio-transcription/tool-rows.json and tools/audio-transcription/test/hear-a-link.test.mjs (a page with captions answers its captions without fetching the sound): the stand-in link reader reports title Sample garden talk, duration 12.5 and writes a two-cue captions.en.vtt. The answer was worked out from read-data/hear-here.mjs (hearALink, captionWords), not run here.
